$comment: Disagreements between the corpus and the published contract, or with a merged artifact that is not a registered adapter. These are recorded, not repaired: this issue may not change a published schema or another ticket's implementation. Every row names the issue that owns the decision.

gaps.title: The `sourceLocus` path pattern cannot compile under RE2
gaps.consequence: RE2 — the engine behind the Rust `regex` crate and Go's `regexp` — has no lookahead, so the Rust backend of issue #21 cannot compile the published schema as written and must hand-write the check, which is a second place for the rule to drift.
gaps.corpusDisposition: The oracle validates the locus structurally rather than by the pattern when it decides whether a locus is usable, and records the divergence here.

gaps.title: The published diagnostic has no member for a location inside the document
gaps.finding: `common.schema.json#/$defs/diagnostic` is sealed with `additionalProperties: false` and locates only by `locus`, a source-file position.
gaps.consequence: A JSON-level checker, and every negative fixture that addresses a node, has nowhere contract-defined to put an RFC 6901 instance pointer. The merged readers invented a dotted `path`; this corpus carries an RFC 6901 `pointer` beside the diagnostic rather than inside it. Two implementations will disagree on where that information lives.
gaps.corpusDisposition: The corpus keeps the published diagnostic verbatim and carries `pointer` as corpus metadata beside it.

gaps.title: The named canonical form is not defined
gaps.finding: `contracts-v1.md` names `RFC8785-JCS-with-identity-sorted-sets-v1` and `package-lock.schema.json` fixes it as a constant, but no artifact defines what an identity-sorted set is or how it is serialized.
gaps.consequence: Two conforming implementations can produce different fingerprints for the same input, which defeats the determinism the fingerprint exists to prove.
gaps.corpusDisposition: The corpus names its own comparison form `agent-ix-conformance-jcs-v1` and states in `README.md` that it is not the fingerprint form, so no reader mistakes one for the other.

gaps.title: Three constructs issue #20 names have no IR node
gaps.finding: Issue #20's deliverables list generics, renames, and deprecations. The IR has no node for a generic type parameter, no rename record, and no deprecation member.
gaps.consequence: There is nothing to write a construct-register row against, so those three deliverables cannot be covered by any case.
gaps.corpusDisposition: Recorded here rather than as a register row, per FR-038. Generic instantiation is representable only by minting one type per instantiation, which loses the parameter.

gaps.title: `resultState` carries values no rule assigns
gaps.finding: `common.schema.json#/$defs/resultState` admits `partial` and `unsupported`; `contracts-v1.md` says an invalid, unsupported, or unavailable result emits zero files and at least one diagnostic, but nothing says when a compiler returns `partial` rather than `lossy`, or `unsupported` rather than `invalid`.
gaps.consequence: Two conforming compilers can return different states for one input and both cite the contract.
gaps.corpusDisposition: The oracle returns only `success`, `invalid`, and `lossy`, which FR-036 declares exhaustive and disjoint for a verdict, and leaves `partial`, `unsupported`, and `unavailable` to the adapter layer.

gaps.title: A consumer policy cannot say which capabilities it admits
gaps.finding: `common.schema.json#/$defs/extension` carries `capability`, and `contracts-v1.md` says unknown required capabilities fail; `consumer-policy.schema.json` has `unknownExtensions` and `exports` but no capability member.
gaps.consequence: The rule 'a required capability no consumer admits fails' has no expressible input, so it cannot be checked as written.
gaps.corpusDisposition: The oracle decides the reachable half — a required extension whose identity the policy does not list while it rejects unknown extensions — and records that the capability half is unexpressible.

gaps.title: The constraint applicability table is named but not published
gaps.finding: `contracts-v1.md` says the keyword set carries 'typed operands per keyword and an applicability table over the resolved kind'. No artifact publishes the table.
gaps.consequence: Every implementation reconstructs it, and this corpus reconstructed it too. A disagreement between two backends about whether `nonEmpty` applies to a map is a disagreement about an unpublished rule.
gaps.corpusDisposition: The oracle's table is written down in `conformance/oracle/oracle.mjs` and exercised by the constraint family, so at least one reading is testable; it is not authority.

gaps.title: The unknown-policy tightening direction is not ordered
gaps.finding: `contracts-v1.md` calls unknown-policy tightening breaking; `common.schema.json#/$defs/unknownPolicy` lists `preserve`, `reject`, and `surface` with no ordering.
gaps.consequence: Whether `preserve` to `surface` is a tightening is undecided, so two compatibility classifiers can disagree.
gaps.corpusDisposition: The oracle treats a move to `reject` as breaking and any other change as conditional, and states so in FR-036; the ordering is the corpus's reading, not the contract's.

gaps.title: The resolution rule for a `reference` kind's target is unstated
gaps.finding: `contracts-v1.md` states a resolution rule for relationship targets only — "Relationship targets resolve to a document type or a lock export" — and states none for the `target` of a `reference`-kind type definition, which the schema requires but constrains only to the semanticIdentity pattern.
gaps.consequence: The issue #19 compiler, compiled read-only over its own `test/fixtures/compiler/packages/assurance` fixture, emits `ix://agent-ix/assurance/type/ActorRef` as a `reference` whose target is `ix://agent-ix/core/type/Actor`. No type in the document declares that identity, the manifest declares no imports, and no lock export names it. Issue #19's own reader accepts the document (`inspect` exits 0 and reports 18 types); this oracle rejects it with one `UNRESOLVED_TYPE_REF` at `/ir/types/0/target`. Both readings are defensible against the contract as written, so two conforming implementations disagree about whether the document is valid — and a generated-package backend must decide whether to emit a type for a reference it cannot resolve.
gaps.corpusDisposition: Ruled by ADR-0009 (accepted): a target — a relationship's or a `reference`-kind definition's — resolves to a document type, a lock export, or an export named by a declared manifest import, and is refused otherwise. `contracts-v1.md` now states that rule for both kinds. The oracle's reading is upheld; the `assurance` fixture is defective because it declares `"imports": []` while naming a type from another package, not because the contract lacked a way to say so. No schema change. REF-001..004 stay as authored and no `corpusVersion` bump is owed: read against the ruling, all four expected results are the rule rather than a pre-ruling reading of it. The row stays `open` because the issue #19 reader does not implement the rule — `readContractIr` resolves a field's `typeRef` and never a definition's own `target`, `items` or `values` — which `conformance/divergences.json` records against ALIAS-002, REF-002, SEQMAP-002, UNION-002 and IDENT-005. Issue #52 carried the fixture repair and is closed. Issue #19 was also closed, but without implementing this rule; the reader repair is now tracked as PLAT-859 (Linear), not issue #19.
